outcome: The same platform extends into cloud infrastructure, giving the insurer disaster recovery and burst capacity without rewriting a single workload.
overview: An insurer wanting disaster recovery or burst capacity in cloud usually finds the same obstacle: the workloads would have to be refactored to run there, and refactoring for a scenario that may never occur is hard to justify. Nutanix Cloud Clusters runs the same platform on dedicated cloud infrastructure, so a workload moves without being rewritten. The trade is explicit and worth stating: dedicated infrastructure is billed by the hour whether or not it is doing anything, so the cost model is closer to renting a data centre than to consuming a cloud service.

benefits.text: Workloads move to cloud without refactoring because the platform is the same on both sides
benefits.limits: Portability is of the workload, not of its dependencies; integrations to on-premises systems still have to be reachable from the cloud side

benefits.text: Disaster recovery capacity can exist without a second physical facility
benefits.limits: A dormant cluster still incurs infrastructure cost; a pilot-light design reduces it and lengthens recovery time, and the trade should be chosen deliberately

benefits.text: One operating model covers both locations rather than two skill sets
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance rather than from host counts or invoice history; a design built on the latter is a quotation with an architecture attached

residency: Runs on dedicated infrastructure in a chosen cloud region; the region is a design decision and, for a regulated insurer, the decisive one

notFor.situation: An estate able to refactor its workloads to cloud-native services
notFor.why: Native services are cheaper to run than dedicated infrastructure once the refactoring is done

notFor.situation: A recovery requirement satisfied by an existing second facility
notFor.why: The cost model here is renting infrastructure, which rarely beats a facility already paid for

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Nutanix implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a replicating cloud cluster with a first tested recovery
Support model: Vendor software support plus the cloud provider’s infrastructure support; Redington coordinates both vendor cases.
1) Review — recovery objectives, dependency map, regulatory position on the cloud region
2) Design — warm and pilot-light options priced over the term, replication scope and schedule
3) Build — cloud cluster provisioned, replication running
4) Test and hand over — recovery tested including dependencies, schedule handed over
deliverables: A recovery test brings the defined workload set into service on the cloud cluster
On-premises dependencies are demonstrably reachable during the test, or their absence is recorded
Measured recovery time is reported against the design chosen and its standing cost
effort: 8–12 weeks to a replicating cloud cluster with a first tested recovery
